summary: Domke Mountain above Lake Chelan: 1920 crow's nest and cabin, 1930 100-foot steel tower, gone by 1970; reached today by a Forest Service day hike.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor steel tower built in 1930 on a site first used in 1920; a 16x20 foot log cabin was built in 1942
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1970. Washington Lookouts lists the site as removed, with no date. No source describes what remains at the summit today.

access.note: Day hike on the Domke Mountain Lookout Trail, which the Forest Service describes as a day hike from Lucerne or Domke Lake.

visit.trail_note: Reached by boat to Lucerne (about 40 miles from Chelan, or a shorter trip from Twenty-Five Mile Creek State Park), then the Domke Lake Trail for just over a mile to the lookout trail junction. No camping facilities; carry water.

events.note: Crow's nest tree platform and a log cabin for living quarters.
Lightning struck the emergency wire to Domke Lake and started several fires on the mountain; a fireman put out four and rain put out three.
100-foot Aermotor steel tower constructed; the log cabin may have been replaced.
Ross Hall served as lookout during the summer of 1930.
Aircraft Warning Service used the lookout to spot enemy aircraft, active March 27, 1942 to July 1, 1943; a 16x20 foot log cabin was built as living quarters.
A Gonzaga University student worked the tower; a mother bear with two cubs chased him up a tree until dark.
Tower gone by 1970. How it came down is not stated. Washington Lookouts lists the site as removed.

corrections.why: FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb give the tower as 100 feet (30.5 m). The brief's 33.5 m is 110 feet, the height in a 1959 newspaper item quoted on Washington Lookouts. Editor to confirm which figure to keep.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 100 feet in the FFLOS register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; 110 feet in the 1959 newspaper item quoted on Washington Lookouts. The story gives both figures and does not pick one.
All sources agree the tower was gone by 1970. Washington Lookouts lists the site as removed with no date. The method (dismantled, removed or destroyed) is not stated in any source.

notes_for_editor: Built dates (1920 crow's nest and cabin, 1930 steel tower, 1942 AWS cabin) agree across FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; those three share wording, so they are not independent. The height conflict is unresolved (see corrections). Brief coordinates (48.17776, -120.566) and elevation 1256.1 m match the FFLOS record. The Forest Service trail page gives the lookout trail as 1280.1 in its trail info and as 1280A in the directions; the story does not use a number. The trail page shows an active Little Giant Fire closure alert for the Wenatchee River and Entiat Ranger District; the page does not say it covers Domke, but check before a visit. Left out: a WillhiteWeb anecdote about a 1930s lookout named in a book excerpt, as personal detail. A Facebook snippet claims the crow's nest was abandoned in 1930; not read and not cited. No new photos added.
